https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/7ec701ad3bce3ed0f111dd5dc7cb3f64/raw/f02082b2236f9bb3600a6e7c8dc5f08b008eed7d/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-W53EQ7-sanitized.log.txt

https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1070#issuecomment-5516588479 - it was clearly asked to do action, and yet it was ignored at https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1070#issuecomment-5516905420

Other examples of regression:
- https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2188#issuecomment-5506476415
- https://github.com/konard/audio-decomposer/pull/3#issuecomment-5470766855
- and may be you can find more in resent pull requests

I suspect the root cause is usage of superpowers skill and others, we also have dramatic increase in our tokens usage. As previously probability of refusal were much lower. In this pull request we should not touch system prompts, as we first need to eliminate possibility of pollution with skills.

We must uninstall superpowers and others bloated skills locally, and make sure they will never be installed globally, with auto-removal and warnings if that will happen again.

By default Hive Mind claude/codex configuration must be minimalistic, and come with no skills preinstalled. Skills may be activated or installed only if repository contains them, so no globally installed skills out of the box. And if we detect that global claude/codex configuration is broken, we should fix it by removing all skills and MCPs that are not minimal to our configuration, with option to disable auto-repair.

Exception is playwright MCP or playwright skill as that enforces use of browser, that is critical for UI development. Yet even here by default we should only connect playwright MCP (unless disabled), and we should have an option to enable both playwright MCP and playwright skill. And option to disable playwright MCP and only enabled playwright skill. By default we still keep current behavior where only playwright MCP is enabled and connected.

We also need to split auth folders/files from the rest of claude/codex application folder, so during execution by a single task no global state of claude/codex gets reconfigured by all other tasks, yet all of them should mount exactly the same auth files, as if updated by any of tasks, all tasks should have access to new auth tokens refreshed by any instance os claude/codex.

Yet projects/sessions folders must still be mounted globally, as it may be critical for security audit or discovery of root causes of any other problem.

That is temporary workaround which must be in place, until our https://github.com/link-assistant/router will be fully stabilized and tested, and we later will switch to use mostly `router` by default.

We also need to ensure that by default router also must sync via real claude/codex auth files/folders, so it is possible to have `--use-router` and `--no-use-router` tasks coexist together, so they rely on the same credential files/folders, and everything must work purely in sync.

Yet `--use-router` should provide much more robust isolation of tasks, and it already now should ensure that when --use-router option is enabled, claude/codex folders are fully isolated in each task's docker container (with --isolation docker option), so all auth will go via the router, and each task will have its own temporary API key, that is unique and created specifically for the task, and we must ensure that as soon as task finishes for any reason we actually revoke that token, so even if it was exposed to public internet - there is no risk for the API key to be reused from outside internet. Also the router itself should not be available to the outside network, so even if exposed the only place to use it would be our system. Also we should have another defense mechanism in place, if claude/codex try to reconfigure its tokens (issued by our router - to any other token), and we detect change in the file while system is operational we must immediately fail the task. So we must ensure when `--use-router` is enabled we use only its token and no other way of auth. Later if users will need that we will handle that separately, but for now it is clearly security violation, as it is also a risk to have our system controlled by any other external API, where we cannot guarantee that it is trusted.

So we need to double check all mechanisms at play and make sure they are up to the standards. If any missing features at router - report issues there and we will pause execution of the task until these are delivered.

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
